questions.question: The International Day of the Girl Child is observed every year across the world on _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11 October**__.

questions.question: The levels of glycated hemoglobin in blood are influenced by many factors. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Glycated Haemoglobin** **or A1C Haemoglobin (HbA1C)** is a type of Haemoglobin.
 
• The process of attachment of sugar to haemoglobin is called **Glycation**.
 
• Hence, glycated haemoglobin is the haemoglobin which has a sugar (generally glucose) attached to it.
 
• **HbA1C test** is a popular test to **detect diabetes** as glyacted haemoglobin is easiest to detect.
 
• Higher amount of HbA1C indicates higher level of blood sugar levels, leading to diabetes.
 
• **Many factors can alter the HbA1C levels like-__**
 
 
• Blood loss, blood transfusion, anaemia, Iron deficiency, Pregnancy, high dose of Vitamin C etc.
 
 

Hence, option 4 is correct.

questions.question: Metamorphosis in frogs is controlled by:
questions.solution:
__

• Metamorphosis in a frog involves amazing transformation from a fish like tadpole to an adult frog.
 
• **The life cycle of a frog is: __**

• The **Thyroxin hormone** in **Thyroid gland** of the tadpole initiates the process of metamorphosis.

questions.question: Marginal cost is directly proportional to its ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. __**Variable costs**__

__
 
• **Marginal cost is directly proportional ****to its Variable costs.**
 
• Marginal cost is the **increase in the total cost when one more product is produced**.
 
• In other words, it is the cost incurred in producing one more unit of goods.
 
• **Fixed costs** are costs that do not depend upon the output or number of units produced.
 
• The rent of a Factory does not depend upon the number of units produced and hence is a Fixed cost.
 
• **Thus, the marginal cost is directly proportional to the variable cost.**
 
• **For Example:-**__
 
 
• Space is rented to make wooden doors. The rent of the space is the Fixed cost.
 
• The cost of labour and the cost of wood are variable costs and depend upon the number of units to be produced.
 
• Thus, the marginal cost to produce one more unit of a door will include labour cost and cost of wood and not the rent of the space, which is a fixed cost and has already been paid for, irrespective of the output.

questions.question: Which gas, in its solid state, is known as dry ice?

• Dry Ice is mainly used for** food preservation.**
 
• It can also be used for making carbonated beverages and ice creams.

questions.question: Ilbert Bill, which was introduced by ______, is a controversial measure proposed in 1883.

• Earlier only European judges could try European offenders.
 
• The bill was introduced by the then-viceroy, Lord Ripon.
 
• The bill had to face intense criticism from the Europeans and Britishers as they looked it as a humiliation as it placed Indian judges at par with European Judges.
 
• The bill was named after the framer of the bill, Courtenay Ilbert, who was appointed as legal adviser to the Council of India.
 
• It was withdrawn due to opposition in Britain and from British settlers in India and was reintroduced in a much-diluted state.
 
• Extra:-

questions.question: In January 2019, researchers from _______ revealed that they had recreated space fuel by simulating interstellar conditions in the laboratory.
questions.solution:
• In January 2019, researchers from **Indian Institute of Technology-Madras (IIT-M)** revealed that they had recreated *“**space fuel”*** by simulating interstellar conditions in the laboratory.
 
• The research suggests that deep space could be the future source of energy and fuel for Earth.
 
• The research tried forming **Clathrate hydrates (CHs) **in an environment simulating deep space.
 
• **Clathrate hydrates or gas hydrates** are water molecules in which gases like methane and CO₂ etc are trapped in the structure of water molecule.
 
• CHs have been found in marine sea beds and permafrost regions of earth, however, presence of CHs in deep space is still unknown.
 
• The experiment could successfully create CHs in an environment imitating interstellar conditions.
 
• Thus, the experiment suggests the likely presence of gases like Methane, CO₂ etc in the deep space.
 
• CHs present in deep space could in future be used to extract gases like methane and CO₂ from them and these gases can be used as a fuel on earth

questions.question: Aurobindo Ghose was born in Calcutta (now Kolkata) on _______
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Aurobindo Ghose (Sri Aurobindo) was born in Calcutta (now Kolkata) on 15th August 1872.**
 
• He was a yogi, guru, poet, Indian philosopher and an Indian freedom fighter.
 
• He was a part of **Anushilan Samiti, **an organisation which supported revolutionary violence for ending British Rule.
 
• Aurobindo was arrested and tried in **Alipore Bomb case in 1908**
 
• He was eventually set free after which he retired from active politics and moved to **Pondicherry** choosing spiritual path.
 
• He founded the Aurobindo Ashram in Pondichery in 1926.
 
• Some of his Literary works are:
 
 
• ***The life Divine***, ***The synthesis of Yoga*** and ***Savitri***

 
 
 

 
• **Extra:-__ Alipore Bomb Case*** ​*

 
 
• **Lord Curzon**, the then Viceroy of India **partitioned Bengal in 1905**.
 
• As a retaliation, in response in **1908**, **Khudiram Bose** and **Prafulla Chaki** threw a bomb at Magistrate Kingsford.
 
• But the bomb instead of Kingsford, killed two british woman.
 
• The above incidence is known as the **Alipore Bomb case**.
 
• Aurobindo, Khudiram Bose, Prafulla Chaki and others were arrested and tried in the Alipore Bomb Case.
